title: Rosalind and the Landfall
premise: Mirabel Quintana, a salvage diver on the storm-bitten coast of Isla Verde, is hired to quietly recover a navy wreck that officially doesn't exist. When an earthquake tide exposes a sea cave beneath the wreck, Mirabel and a small expedition crew discover a preserved colonial settlement — and evidence that Mirabel's own grandmother helped seal it decades ago. As the navy moves to bury the find and a rival salvager circles, the crew must document and protect the cave before it's dynamited shut forever. In the end, Mirabel chooses public truth over inherited silence, releasing the records at the cost of their salvage license but winning the island its history back.
about_author: Lena Villalobos is a former maritime archaeologist who spent six years cataloguing wrecks in the Caribbean before turning to fiction full-time. She writes adventure novels from a houseboat, drawing on real expeditions and the oral histories of coastal communities.

chapters.title: The Wreck Nobody Names
chapters.summary: Mirabel dives a charted-as-empty reef and finds a naval hull stamped with a serial number that matches no registry. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: unease — the first crack in the official story they've always trusted.

chapters.title: Salt Ledger
chapters.summary: Back ashore, Mirabel's employer, a navy liaison named Commander Reyes, pays double for silence and forbids further dives. Mirabel's grandmother's old dive logs hint she worked these waters too. POV: Mirabel. Beat: suspicion taking root alongside grief for her late grandmother.

chapters.title: The Crew of Strays
chapters.summary: Mirabel assembles a small team: engineer Tomas, archivist Yolanda, and diver-protege Kip, each with debts or dreams that make them say yes. POV: rotating crew. Beat: found-family warmth before the storm.

chapters.title: Low Tide, High Warning
chapters.summary: A minor offshore quake drains the reef unusually far; Kip spots a dark opening beneath the wreck. Reyes warns Mirabel off by radio mid-dive. POV: Mirabel. Beat: temptation versus obedience.

chapters.title: Admission Charged in Legends
chapters.summary: Island elders tell Mirabel the cave is 'the mouth that takes payment' — divers who entered never surfaced whole. One elder recognizes Mirabel's surname and goes quiet. POV: Mirabel. Beat: dread braided with belonging.

chapters.title: First Descent
chapters.summary: Against orders, the crew enters the cave at slack tide, finding air pockets, carved stone stairs, and a chamber of intact colonial structures. POV: Kip. Beat: awe curdling into claustrophobia as the tide begins returning.

chapters.title: What the Water Kept
chapters.summary: Yolanda documents ledgers and letters suggesting the settlement was deliberately flooded, not lost. A name recurs in the records: Quintana. POV: Yolanda. Beat: the personal colliding with the historical.

chapters.title: Reyes' Deadline
chapters.summary: Commander Reyes gives Mirabel 72 hours to finish 'recovery' before demolition charges close the site permanently. Rival salvager Dario Cruz offers to buy their intel. POV: Mirabel. Beat: pressure mounting from every side.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Logbook
chapters.summary: In a locked sea chest, Mirabel finds her grandmother's 1960s logbook describing the same cave — and a decision to help seal it 'for the island's own good.' POV: Mirabel. Beat: betrayal and inheritance entwined.

chapters.title: Dario's Price
chapters.summary: Cruz's crew shadows the expedition boat; a night confrontation ends with Tomas injured and equipment stolen. POV: Tomas. Beat: fear and loyalty tested under fire.

chapters.title: The Second Chamber
chapters.summary: Deeper exploration reveals a sealed vault with a manifest listing what was hidden and why — cargo the navy has hunted for sixty years. POV: Yolanda. Beat: revelation raising stakes from history to present danger.

chapters.title: Tide Trap
chapters.summary: An unexpected swell traps three crew members inside as the entrance floods; Mirabel must navigate uncharted siphons to reach them. POV: Mirabel. Beat: terror, competence, and the cost of secrets.

chapters.title: Resurface
chapters.summary: They surface battered to find Reyes waiting on their dock with arrest authority and Cruz whispering in his ear. POV: Kip. Beat: cornered — the law itself now the adversary.

chapters.title: The Choice of Silence
chapters.summary: Reyes offers Mirabel everything: licenses restored, debts cleared, if the crew signs nondisclosure and walks away. Mirabel sees their grandmother made this same bargain. POV: Mirabel. Beat: the inheritance of silence offered again.

chapters.title: Kip's Evidence
chapters.summary: Kip reveals they secretly copied the manifest and photographed the chambers; Yolanda drafts a disclosure plan using archival law to force review. POV: Kip. Beat: hope rekindled through quiet defiance.

chapters.title: Storm Front
chapters.summary: A hurricane shifts course toward the island; both navy demolition and the expedition are racing the weather. Cruz makes a desperate solo dive for the vault. POV: Tomas. Beat: nature forcing everyone's hand.

chapters.title: Cruz Down
chapters.summary: Mirabel rescues Cruz from a cave-in he caused, learning he was coerced by debts to Reyes' superiors. An uneasy alliance forms. POV: Mirabel. Beat: mercy as strategy and principle.

chapters.title: Last Window
chapters.summary: With the storm hours out, the crew makes a final dive to retrieve the original settlement charter — legal proof the land belongs to the islanders, not the navy. POV: Yolanda. Beat: purpose sharpened to a single point.

chapters.title: Demolition Day
chapters.summary: Reyes' charges are set as the storm arrives; Mirabel confronts him in the surf with the charter and her grandmother's logbook, demanding he read what sealing the cave cost the last generation. POV: Mirabel. Beat: climax — truth against command.

chapters.title: The Sea Decides
chapters.summary: The hurricane surge collapses part of the cliff, destroying the demolition rig and sealing half the cave naturally while sparing the main chamber. Reyes, shaken, stands down. POV: Reyes. Beat: humbling — the wilderness forgives nothing.

chapters.title: Landfall
chapters.summary: Aftermath: the charter triggers a heritage review; the island claims the site; Mirabel loses the salvage license but gains a museum post cataloguing the find with the crew. POV: Mirabel. Beat: belonging earned through loss.

chapters.title: What We Leave Open
chapters.summary: Months later, Mirabel opens the cave as a protected site, placing their grandmother's logbook beside the charter — memory inherited honestly at last. Final image: the tide withdrawing, the mouth open. POV: Mirabel. Beat: resolution — inheritance rewritten.
